back: Immediate actions after a hazard event: search and rescue, first aid, shelter, food and water.
Long-term actions: rebuilding homes and infrastructure, restoring jobs and services, improving building codes.
Seismometers (small earthquakes), tiltmeters and GPS (ground swelling), gas sampling (SO₂, CO₂), satellites (movement, heat).
Deep foundations, base isolators, cross-braced steel frames, counterweight dampers, shatterproof glass, automatic gas shut-off.
Hazard mapping, land-use zoning, evacuation plans, drills and education, emergency kits.
25 April 2015, magnitude 7.8, collision boundary (Indo-Australian and Eurasian plates); about 9,000 deaths; landslides and slow rebuilding in remote areas.
Philippines, destructive boundary; monitoring led to evacuation of tens of thousands; about 800-900 deaths, many from ash-laden roofs collapsing; lahars for years; global cooling of about 0.5 °C.
Adding strengthening features to existing buildings so they withstand earthquakes.
